title: Outer dataset view: five ways to compare configs
brief: Open a robot's site and see at a glance which pipeline config (controller) does best across all targets, by how much, where the trade-offs are, and get from there to the targets and runs behind it. Today the UR5e page opens on 9 tiles, 20 bar-group charts and 3 tables: 206,472 px tall at 1440 px wide (229 screens).
defaultWhy: V1 League table scores 84/100: it is the only direction that puts the ranking and its size (×best on a log bar) above the fold while keeping all four scorecard KPIs, with a two-click drill to a run and n on every number. V2 Pareto frontier (80) is the closest alternative and wins when the trade-off itself is the question; V5 Head-to-head (79) gives the fairest 'best overall'.
decisionHinge: What 'best overall' means. V1 and V2 judge each split at full speed from the scorecard, where ctc_tuned leads; V5 pairs configs target by target, where id_pd beats ctc_tuned on 377 of 504 shared targets and loses only at full speed (1.08×). Move 10 points from 'Config verdict at a glance' to 'Trade-offs visible' and V2 leads (82 vs 80); move 10 from 'Compact' to 'Generalises' and V5 comes within one point of V1 (85 vs 86).
invariants: Real data: the bench's UR5e site (4 configs, 1006 targets, 4932 lines, sim only) plus its scorecard charts; no invented numbers.
traj_compare's stack: static pages, vanilla JS + uPlot, traj_compare's own CSS, opening from file:// with no CDN and no build step; config colours from levels.configs.
Tabs on every variant; today's Target level (index.html#/target/<slug>) and run reports stay reachable.
boundary: Five static prototypes on the real UR5e data (extract.py → data/ur5e.js), opened from file://. Real: every number, every control, the Targets and Runs tabs, and the links into the bench's server on 127.0.0.1:8779. Not done: integration into traj_compare's dataset.js; other tabs are thin.

axes.name: Unit of comparison
values: scorecard median per split (V1, V2, V3)

axes.name: What the Overview carries
values: 4 KPIs for one split + RMS of every split (V1)

axes.name: Drill entry
values: dot or config → worst targets at that speed (V2)
chart cell → config at the cursor's speed (V3)

requirements.name: Config verdict at a glance
requirements.why: Zach's ask: 'at the highest level we want to be comparing different pipeline configurations vs how they do on all of the targets' — the landing page must answer which config is best before anything else.
requirements.passCondition: Which config is best overall and by how much is readable above the fold at 1440 × 900 with no scroll or click.

anchors.1: Must scroll and read many charts.
anchors.3: Visible, but needs reading several numbers.
anchors.5: One glance: ranking and magnitude explicit.

requirements.name: Compact
requirements.why: 'WAYYY too hard to navigate … more compact': today's scorecard alone is about 15 screens.
requirements.passCondition: The scorecard's content (4 KPIs × datasets/splits × 5 speeds × configs) fits the Overview tab.

requirements.name: Trade-offs visible
requirements.why: 'Pareto graphs and line charts may be more compact' — configs trade error against energy, jerk and speed.
requirements.passCondition: Shows how configs trade error against cost (energy, jerk, speed).

anchors.3: Several metrics side by side, no joint view.
anchors.5: An explicit joint view or frontier.

requirements.name: Drill path
requirements.why: The outer view is a doorway: from a verdict to the targets that explain it and the run that shows it.
requirements.passCondition: From a config or a point to the targets where it does worst, then a run.

anchors.3: A link to an unfiltered list.
anchors.5: Click: filtered worst targets, then the run.

requirements.name: Generalises
requirements.why: The bench writes one site per robot; the outer view is traj_compare's, not UR5e's.
requirements.passCondition: Works for 4 configs sim-only (UR5e), 11 configs (BAM FB) and sim + real (pendulum) from traj_compare's generic payload plus the optional summary.

requirements.name: Truthful
requirements.why: Zach reads numbers literally; an unlabelled median over an unstated set is a trap.
requirements.passCondition: Every number traceable to the payload or the bench scorecard, units shown, n stated, aggregation named.

anchors.5: Every number labelled with source and n.

hardGates.name: Real UR5e data, nothing fabricated
hardGates.why: A layout judged on invented numbers proves nothing about the real site.

hardGates.name: Runs from file:// with no network
hardGates.why: traj_compare sites open from disk; a CDN or fetch would break that.

variants.name: League table
variants.thesis: One ranked row per config — tool RMS at full speed with ×best on a log bar, then gates, energy and jerk beside their curves against speed — and a rank matrix of every split below.
variants.bestWhen: You want the answer and its size in one read, and the scorecard's four KPIs stay the vocabulary.
variants.losesWhen: The winner changes with speed (on UR5e id_pd wins below full speed): the table answers per split at full speed, so you switch chips or read the matrix.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: A ranked row per config: rank, n, ×best, a log bar for the distance.

decisions.label: Aggregation
decisions.value: The scorecard's median over the split's tasks at full speed; splits the scorecard lacks are filled from the payload, in italic.

decisions.label: Navigation
decisions.value: Dataset · split chips and a click-to-switch rank matrix; a Speed sweeps tab holds the full curves.

decisions.label: Drill
decisions.value: A row opens that config's worst targets on the split at full speed.

keepParts: log bar of the distance to the best
proof: Opened from file:// at 1440 × 900 on the UR5e data: Overview one screen tall, 0 console errors, 0 network requests.
Clicked the workspace-v2 dev chip, then ctc_model_err's 'worst targets →': the Targets tab filtered to ctc_model_err · workspace-v2 dev · speed 1.0.
The same file on BAM FB and the pendulum via ?site=, no code changes.

fr1.evidence: Verdict line plus ranked rows with ×best above the fold: ctc_tuned 0.0357 mm, id_pd 1.2×, ctc_model_err 25×, menagerie_stock 1,526×; 'lowest RMS in 24 of 40 cells' adds the across-split answer. The verdict is per split at full speed.

fr2.evidence: The Overview is one screen but holds 80 of the scorecard's 300 values (the chosen split) plus 24 full-speed RMS cells in the matrix; the other splits are one chip click each.

fr3.evidence: Four KPIs side by side per config with sparklines; no joint view — id_pd's half energy (14.8 J vs 28.4 J) is in the verdict text, not a plot.

fr4.evidence: Row → Targets filtered to config, split and full speed, worst first → run ↗: 2 clicks, exercised; the run and Target links answered 200 from the bench's server.

fr5.evidence: Same code on BAM FB and the pendulum; its table is scorecard-bound, so BAM FB's 9 non-scorecard configs appear only in the matrix (payload, italic), and the pendulum's 8 series make it 1144 px.

fr6.evidence: n column, 'median over the split's tasks' in the headers, scorecard vs payload marked per cell, and the oracle line (120 of 120 scorecard RMS cells reproduced within 1 %).

g1.evidence: data/ur5e.js from extract.py; its per-target values reproduce 120 of 120 scorecard RMS cells within 1 %.

g2.evidence: Loads only relative files (data/, assets/); Playwright saw 0 non-file requests.

generality.bam_fb: BAM FB (11 configs): the table shows the 2 configs the scorecard has (hold_friction, record); the matrix adds the payload-only configs in italic, and the footnote says 37 scorecard cells have no runs behind them.
generality.pendulum: Pendulum (sim + rehearsal + real): 8 config · domain rows, sim dashed and rehearsal dotted; the page grows to 1144 px.

variants.name: Pareto frontier
variants.thesis: Tool error (log) against energy or jerk, each config a path through its five speeds, with the non-dominated frontier drawn at the chosen speed.
variants.bestWhen: The choice is a trade-off — accuracy against energy or smoothness — and a dominated config should drop out at sight.
variants.losesWhen: A site's scorecard lacks the cost KPI for most configs (BAM FB: 2 of 11), or many configs sit on one point (the pendulum).

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: The error × cost plane; each config a path through its speeds.

decisions.label: Aggregation
decisions.value: Scorecard medians per dev split; the frontier recomputed at the chosen speed.

decisions.label: Navigation
decisions.value: Speed and cost-axis switches, plus thumbnails of the four dev splits.

decisions.label: Drill
decisions.value: A dot or a config opens its worst targets at that split and speed.

proof: Overview: frontier, list and thumbnails in one screen (901 px), 0 console errors, 0 network requests.
Walked speed 1.0 → 0.25 (the frontier shrinks to id_pd), energy → jerk, then clicked ctc_model_err → its worst targets at workspace-v1 dev · 0.25.
The same file on BAM FB and the pendulum.

fr1.evidence: The verdict names the frontier at speed 1.0 (ctc_tuned 0.0357 mm at 28.4 J; id_pd 1.2× the RMS for 0.52× the energy) and what dominates the rest; 'best' is a set, not a rank, and it changes with speed.

fr2.evidence: One screen, but it shows RMS × energy for one dev split (40 values) plus shape-only thumbnails for the other three; jerk is a toggle; the 4 holdout RMS charts are not on the Overview.

fr3.evidence: An explicit joint view: tool RMS (log) × energy or jerk, the frontier as a staircase per speed, dominated points hollow, gate failures ringed red.

fr4.evidence: Dot or config → its worst targets at that split and speed → run ↗: 2 clicks, exercised.

fr5.evidence: Needs the cost KPI in the scorecard: on BAM FB only 2 of 11 configs can be drawn; on the pendulum 8 paths crowd near 1 mm (labels nudged apart). Generic code, data-bound.

fr6.evidence: The verdict and tooltips state 'medians over n tasks' and the source; the side list's numbers carry units but not n.

g1.evidence: Every point is a scorecard median copied by extract.py; nothing interpolated.

g2.evidence: Hand-drawn SVG, relative files only; 0 non-file requests.

generality.bam_fb: BAM FB: only hold_friction and record carry energy in the scorecard, so 2 of 11 configs are drawn; the footnote says so.
generality.pendulum: Pendulum: 8 config · domain paths crowd near 1 mm; labels are nudged apart with leader lines. Energy falls with speed here.

variants.name: Small multiples
variants.thesis: Today's 20 bar-group charts as one screen of small line charts — rows are KPI × split, columns are datasets, one line per config, one shared legend and one y scale per row.
variants.bestWhen: You want the whole scorecard in one glance and to see how every KPI moves with speed.
variants.losesWhen: You need one answer or the size of a gap: it shows everything and ranks only in the verdict's counts.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: The scorecard itself, redrawn as lines against speed.

decisions.label: Aggregation
decisions.value: Scorecard medians; one y range per row (log for RMS and jerk).

decisions.label: Navigation
decisions.value: Legend focus plus a cursor synced across all 20 charts with a value readout.

decisions.label: Drill
decisions.value: A chart opens the focused (or worst) config's targets at the cursor's speed.

Focused id_pd, hovered conveyor-v1 · tool RMS dev (readout with n), clicked → id_pd's worst targets at conveyor-v1 dev · 0.5.
The same file on BAM FB and the pendulum.

variants.name: Config × target heatmap
variants.thesis: Every target is a column and every config a row, coloured by log tool RMS (or ÷ the best config on that target), with a strip of the winner per target.
variants.bestWhen: You want to see where each config wins or breaks across all targets, and to jump straight to one target.
variants.losesWhen: You need the scorecard's energy, jerk or gate numbers: they exist only as split medians and this view has no place for them.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: The full config × target matrix: 1006 columns.

decisions.label: Aggregation
decisions.value: Per target, median over repeats; nothing averaged across targets.

decisions.label: Navigation
decisions.value: Colour mode, order within a block, a domain filter; hover names the target.

decisions.label: Drill
decisions.value: A column opens the real Target level; a config name opens its worst targets against the best.

proof: Overview 646 px, 0 console errors, 0 network requests.
Switched to ratio colour, hovered a workspace-v1 holdout target (tooltip: every config, best first, ×best), clicked menagerie_stock → its worst targets against the best.
The same file on BAM FB (15 rows) and the pendulum (12 rows, domain filter).

fr1.evidence: Verdict: lowest tool RMS on 604 of 1006 targets for ctc_tuned and 359 of 504 for id_pd; menagerie_stock worst on 492 of 504 shared; per-row medians at the right. Ranking explicit, magnitude via colour.

fr2.evidence: One screen (646 px), but none of the scorecard's energy, jerk or gates values, and no other tab carries them; tool RMS appears as 1006 × 4 per-target cells instead.

fr3.evidence: One metric; its growth with speed shows across the speed blocks, but no energy or jerk.

fr4.evidence: Column → its real Target level, then run ↗ (2 clicks); config name → worst targets against the best → run ↗ (2 clicks), exercised.

fr5.evidence: Payload only: BAM FB shows all 15 config · domain rows, the pendulum gets a domain filter; no per-robot code.

fr6.evidence: Every row: median of n targets and best-on count; the tooltip lists repeat counts; the colour scale is labelled in mm or ×best.

g1.evidence: Cells are per-target medians over repeats of the payload's per-run values.

g2.evidence: Canvas drawing, relative files only; 0 non-file requests.

generality.bam_fb: BAM FB: all 15 config · domain rows; the fullarm configs with 1–5 runs are slivers in workspace-v2, honest about how little they ran.
generality.pendulum: Pendulum: 12 rows; the domain switch (all · sim · rehearsal · real) keeps sim and real from competing in one strip.

variants.name: Head-to-head
variants.thesis: Pick a baseline; every other config becomes the distribution of its per-target tool-RMS ratio to it over the targets both ran — 'better on k of n', the median ratio, and that ratio against speed.
variants.bestWhen: Configs ran different target sets, or you want a fair, paired 'who is better and by how much' instead of medians over different targets.
variants.losesWhen: You need energy, jerk or gates, or one absolute number to quote: everything is relative to the baseline.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: Paired per-target ratios to one baseline config.

decisions.label: Aggregation
decisions.value: Shared targets only; median of the ratios; a 10-target floor.

decisions.label: Navigation
decisions.value: Baseline chips plus an every-pair matrix.

decisions.label: Drill
decisions.value: A row or a pair cell opens that config's targets sorted by ratio to the baseline.

keepParts: better on k of n shared targets
proof: Overview 691 px, 0 console errors, 0 network requests.
Default baseline id_pd → switched to ctc_tuned → clicked id_pd's row → its targets sorted by ratio to ctc_tuned.
The same file on BAM FB and the pendulum.

fr1.evidence: Verdict plus 'better on k of n shared targets' and median ratio per config, e.g. against ctc_tuned: id_pd better on 377 of 504 (0.5×), ctc_model_err 62×, menagerie_stock 2,607×; the pair matrix answers every pair at once.

fr2.evidence: One screen (691 px), but none of the scorecard's energy, jerk or gates; tool RMS appears as per-target ratios.

fr3.evidence: One metric (the RMS ratio) and that ratio against speed per config (id_pd ÷ ctc_tuned rises to 1.08× at full speed); no energy or jerk.

fr4.evidence: Row → that config's targets sorted by ratio to the baseline, worst first → run ↗: 2 clicks, exercised; pair cells drill the same way.

fr5.evidence: Payload only: on BAM FB the 10-target floor turns 1–3-run configs into one-line ratios; on the pendulum sim, rehearsal and real series of the same targets compare directly.

fr6.evidence: Every ratio states k of n shared targets and 'median'; the default-baseline rule is printed with its basis (the 504 targets all four configs ran).

g1.evidence: Ratios of the payload's per-target medians; only targets both configs ran.

g2.evidence: Hand-drawn SVG, relative files only; 0 non-file requests.

generality.bam_fb: BAM FB: default baseline hold_friction_v2 (no target is shared by all well-covered configs, and the verdict says so); configs with 1–3 runs drop below the 10-target floor into one line.
generality.pendulum: Pendulum: sim, rehearsal and real series of one config compare on the same targets, a sim-to-real gap view for free.

checks: Exactly five structural directions, each a different primary object
Same UR5e data, 1440 × 900 viewport and product fidelity for every hero
Criteria and gates frozen in CONTRACT.md before any variant was built
Every score carries evidence and confidence; gates separate from the weighted total
Walkthrough stills and the live iframe drive the same states
